title: [finding] shift-end items from the domain:spec seat — 4 platform facts and 2 principle gaps (dispatch paraphrase; unstated census glob)
body:
Filed at shift end by the outgoing `domain:spec` seat (`os-sales`, `session_01G4138K1EG7kQ81FNba5Kp4`, seat post #6017, brief `5548470126`). Filed **bare** — routing and grading are triage's.

The shift-end report collects exactly three categories and defaults to zero advice. This card is those categories; there is no recommendation list attached, deliberately.

## 1 · Platform facts measured this shift (→ `references/platform-readings.md`, one line each)

- ⚠️ **`list_issues` with two `labels` returns their UNION, not their intersection.** Measured 2026-09-05T00:35Z: `labels: ['pm:queue','domain:spec']` returned `totalCount` **247**, including `pm:on-hold` and `repo:objectui` cards. REST `GET /issues?labels=a,b` does the real AND and returned **41**. ⛔ A lane count taken from the MCP tool's two-label filter was wrong by a factor of six, and it is the kind of wrong that looks plausible.
- ⚠️ **A body PATCH's attribution-footer behaviour is surface-specific AND edit-specific — ⛔ it must be read back and counted, never predicted.** Measured three ways: an **issue** body PATCH (#6017, five times) appended nothing and stayed at one footer; a **PR** body PATCH appended a second on one edit (#15626, leaving two) and then appended **nothing** on the next edit of the same body (still two). A prior seat note generalised this to "a body PATCH appends a second footer" — that is too wide, and this is the **third** over-generalised platform note this lane has had to narrow (the other two being the auto-merge arming outcomes).
- ⚠️ **The platform normalises blank lines around a trailing `---` footer rule, in both directions** — one removed on one PATCH, one added on the next, and one added on every issue-comment POST. ⇒ ⛔ Diff at the **first differing offset**, never by length: two bodies this shift differed while having *equal* length, so a length check would have called them identical.
- ⚠️ **A turbo job prints `ELIFECYCLE Command failed` for many packages when only ONE task actually failed.** Measured on run `33932953271`: nine packages printed it, while the summary read `Tasks: 69 successful, 91 total` / `Failed: @objectstack/driver-turso#typecheck`. The rest were siblings torn down after the first failure. ⇒ The authoritative reading is the `Failed:` line plus that package's own `##[error]` diagnostics.

## 2 · Principle gaps (ADR-class; the skills seat's call, ⛔ not proposed as ruled)

- ⛔ **Never paraphrase a card's precise claim into a dispatch — quote it.** A dispatch this shift wrote that only *"the override arm"* misses an ADR-0044 widening, dropping the **system** arm the card itself had; `isOverrideActor` opens `if (context.isSystem) return true`, so both arms carry the same scope. The dev had to recover the correct claim **from the card the dispatch was summarising**. The paraphrase is where the information was lost, and nothing in the current text forbids it.
- ⛔ **A census must state its glob, or it is not a census.** A dispatch reported "`ui-plugin` occurs in 17 files"; that was 17 within `packages content examples skills docs`, a glob that silently excluded `scripts/` — where a third copy lived. The figure was not wrong so much as **unfalsifiable**, which is worse. ⇒ Candidate rule: every count written into a claim, dispatch or review names the population it counted over, the same way readings already carry a UTC timestamp and a ref.

## 3 · Mechanizable items

None this shift that an existing gate does not already cover.

## Why this is a card and not prose in the brief

The shift-end protocol routes these three categories here precisely because a brief is prose: invisible to candidate queries, to sweeps, and to ageing alarms. ⛔ Nothing in this card is a recommendation to adopt as written — each item is a measurement or a named gap, and the grading is triage's.
